- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is bullish (sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is bearish (sentiment < 0.2) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Lag in correction: model often lags true price movements by 1–3 days, especially after sharp sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows, underestimating volatility in mid-range zones.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overreact to short-term sentiment, underperforming when sentiment stabilizes or reverses.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.5), model tends to err on the high side — adjust downward by 1–2% of forecasted value.
- Spike recovery: after a price spike, model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
